features.item: A housing with a grip portion designed as a hollow body for gripping
An electrically operated vacuum generating device in the housing
Exhaust air from the vacuum generating device guided through the hollow grip portion to an air outlet
A sound-damping device arranged in the grip portion
A suction plate comprising a carrier plate and a seal fastened to the carrier plate extending around it
A grip unit with hollow grip portion, electrically operated vacuum generator, exhaust air routed through grip to outlet, and sound-damping device in grip
Vacuum handling apparatus with suction plate and grip unit combined
Grip portion at least partially lined with sound-damping material
Vacuum generating device arranged completely in a first housing portion
Sound-reducing device in the first housing portion or first housing portion lined with sound-reducing material
Grip portion elongated between first and second housing portions with air outlet on second housing portion
Air collection screw upstream of grip portion in first housing portion for collecting exhaust air
Bent or curved air baffles downstream of grip portion directing exhaust air to air outlet
Battery coupling point on second housing portion with air baffles directing exhaust air away from battery coupling point
Grip unit and suction plate releasably connected via a coupling device
Grip unit with suction opening fluidically connected to suction chamber delimited by suction plate

claims.note: This reference is about an apparatus for inspecting pharmaceutical containers, not a grip unit for a vacuum hand-operated laying device.
This reference is about an apparatus for inspecting pharmaceutical containers and does not disclose a housing with a grip portion or an electrically operated vacuum generating device.
This reference does not describe any grip portion, let alone one designed as a hollow body.
This reference does not disclose a vacuum generating device or exhaust air being guided through a grip portion to an air outlet.
This reference does not disclose a sound-damping device arranged in a grip portion.
This reference does not disclose a grip portion at least partially lined with a sound-damping material.
This reference does not disclose a vacuum generating device arranged completely in a first housing portion.
This reference does not disclose a sound-reducing device arranged in a first housing portion or the first housing portion being lined with sound-reducing material.
This reference does not disclose a grip unit, housing portions, or an air outlet as described in the claim.
This reference does not disclose an air collection device, an air collection screw, or a grip portion.
This reference does not disclose a grip portion, housing portions, or air baffles for guiding exhaust air.
This reference does not disclose a battery coupling point, an electrical energy storage device, a rechargeable battery, or air baffles for directing exhaust air.
This reference does not mention air baffles, exhaust air, or battery coupling points.
This reference describes an apparatus for inspecting pharmaceutical containers, not a vacuum handling apparatus.
This reference does not describe a suction plate, carrier plate, or a seal fastened to a carrier plate.
This reference does not describe a grip unit as defined in claim 1 of the subject invention.
This reference does not disclose a grip unit, a suction plate, or a coupling device for releasably connecting them.
This reference does not disclose a grip unit with a suction opening fluidically connected to a suction chamber to generate a vacuum between a suction plate and an object.

overall.why: The reference describes an apparatus for inspecting pharmaceutical containers with a handling device, support wheels, friction wheel, and specific angular relationships, which aligns with many aspects of the subject claims. However, it does not disclose the specific features related to a hollow grip
